discoveredComplexity: A KV write has three outcomes, not two, and reading it as two is how an index loses a delivery. The sweep had conflated a lost compare-and-set with a refused write everywhere a record was written; the first carries the delivery on in another sweeper's hands and the second carries nothing at all, and only the second must stop the cursor. The same distinction decides whether the back-fill may mark the bucket.

An index field a build may not carry is not a field whose absence means disowned. The record's Pending is absent in two different situations -- an older build rewrote the record, or the record never had an entry -- and in neither is deleting the entry right. Treating absence as adoption, and only a different value as disowning, is what carries a rolling deploy and a rollback.

A repair that deletes on sight races the writer it is repairing after. An entry is written before the record that names it, so an entry keyed in the current minute may be one another sweeper is about to name; the repair must only take entries older than the clock margin the rest of the file already uses.
